mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to decreased consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following an unemployment rate increase above 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate increases while payroll employment remains stable, it may indicate structural issues in the labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following simultaneous increases in UNRATE and stable PAYEMS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate can lead to higher borrowing costs and reduced consumer and business spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following a 0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS during a tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following an increase in HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production indicates reduced economic output, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a drop in INDPRO below 115, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth slows while inflation increases, it may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following simultaneous declines in GDPC1 and increases in CPIAUCSL, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High retail and food services sales indicate strong consumer demand, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following a 5% year-over-year increase in RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.
